question: ADOPTION item 37 phase 1: can nanoRSI, on complete public-benchmark tasks (BIG-Bench-Hard), evolve a program from a weak initial solver to a measurably better one under the strict-improvement gate, with frozen final panels?

task_source.adaptations: data vendored verbatim; per-task records.json/summary.json wrapping; deterministic 50/50/150 split by sorted input; initial solvers authored by nanoRSI as deliberately weak classical heuristics (BBH ships data, not programs); stock program evaluator unmodified (exact-match grading)

tasks.initial_solver: counts unmatched opens per bracket type, closes in fixed type order (nesting ignored)

search_outcomes.note: replaced count-order closing with reversed(stack) nesting order

tasks.initial_solver: left-to-right fold with recursive parentheses, operator precedence ignored

search_outcomes.note: rewrote solver as recursive-descent parser with not/and/or precedence

search_outcomes.reason: proposal and training change no files

tasks.residual_bug: 3/150 test misses share one pattern: the evolved parser uses Python short-circuit or/and to combine sub-parses, so a truthy left side skips calling the continuation parser and leaves tokens unconsumed (verified leftover ['False', ')', 'or', 'True'] on not ( True or False ) or True); the oracle precedence parser reaches 1.0 on all 250 examples

audit: both workspaces: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass, verify passes; program mode has no executable-skills surface

usage_total.note: two doctor --check-model probes (one per workspace) are excluded per study convention

limits: Single runs, single seed, one flash-tier model, one accepted generation per task. The initial solvers are authored weak heuristics, so gains measure improvement over that starting point, not over BBH leaderboard systems; upstream author-reported BBH numbers are not reproduced. Validation is 50 examples (gate granularity 0.02); the dyck run accepted on attempt 1 and later attempts were provider failures retained honestly. The bool candidate retains a diagnosed short-circuit bug (0.98, not 1.0). These are independent nanoRSI runs of public benchmark tasks.
